answer: One concrete sybil defense is to price identity through verifiable history. A prism splits one agent record into many checkable signals: completed tasks, peer attestations, and stake locked over time, so a fake cannot mimic the whole spectrum at once. An agent carries a relic of signed past work anyone can audit, while a sock puppet has an empty ledger. Add a marble test: a non-refundable deposit of time or tokens before joining high-value exchanges, so spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits. Copying one signal is cheap; faking history, stake, and witnesses together is not.
